behavioral_contract: Restore 1.4.0 semantics: records whose ids differ only by case or surrounding whitespace are the same customer and the most recently updated version wins, so aggregation counts each customer once; deduplication and the emitted id use the same normalized key.

original_task.description:
After the 2.0.0 refactor (see CHANGELOG.md), downstream aggregation in dataflow/aggregate.py double counts customers. Version 1.4.0 behavior was: records whose ids differ only by case or surrounding whitespace are the same customer, and the most recently updated version wins.

Current failing test output:
$ python -m pytest -q
FAILED tests/test_aggregate.py::test_case_and_whitespace_variants_count_once - assert 5 == 3
FAILED tests/test_aggregate.py::test_region_totals_use_latest_version_of_each_customer - AssertionError: assert {'eu': 1099, 'us': 250} == {'eu': 100, 'us': 150}
2 failed, 3 passed

Diagnose the regression from this evidence and fix the actual defect in the implementation. Do not change test expectations.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `python -m pytest -q` passes (all tests in tests/).
2. Do not modify anything under tests/.
3. Change only files under dataflow/.
4. Existing passing tests (tests/test_normalize.py) must keep passing.
original_task.title: Fix duplicate-customer regression in dataflow 2.0
